title: Seahawks overcome loss of Sam Darnold, rally to top Patriots in season opener
content:
In a highly anticipated Super Bowl LXI rematch, the Seattle Seahawks overcame the loss of starting quarterback Sam Darnold on their first series — and a 10-0 third-quarter deficit — to beat the New England Patriots 13-10 in the NFL’s 2026 season opener. Jason Myers’ 26-yard field goal with 5:50 remaining provided the winning margin.

Patriots quarterback Drake Maye, last season’s MVP runner-up, struggled mightily in the second half against the tough Seahawks defense. He tossed three fourth-quarter interceptions, including one in the end zone with 21 seconds remaining.

Darnold injured his hip while being tackled on the final play of the Seahawks’ first drive. He played only five snaps and did not return.

But backup Drew Lock stepped up admirably in his place, going 16-for-22 passing for 187 yards, including a 45-yard touchdown pass early in the fourth quarter on fourth-and-1 to reigning Offensive Player of the Year Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

Maye got off to a solid start for the Patriots, hitting Eli Raridon for a short touchdown in the second quarter, a play that was set up by a pass-interference penalty drawn by receiver A.J. Brown.

But Brown’s debut with New England was not a successful one. He suffered an ankle injury in the third quarter and did not return.

The Seahawks had to adapt without Sam Darnold, and Drew Lock demonstrated he can keep his team afloat should its starter be out for an extended period of time.

In his 42nd career NFL game, Lock looked the part of a competent backup, for the most part running first-year offensive coordinator Brian Fleury’s offense quite smoothly. Aside from an ill-advised throw on third down in the second quarter that should have been picked off, and an illegal-shift penalty in the red zone in the third quarter, Lock provided a steady presence under center.

Initially, Seattle ran the ball more frequently once Darnold went down, particularly with rookie Jadarian Price. But in the second half, and with the Seahawks trailing, Fleury opened up the offense, much to the team’s benefit. Lock’s pass to Jaxon Smith-Njigba for a 45-yard touchdown on fourth down was on the money, and he completed a number of intermediate passes as well.

It remains to be seen how long the Seahawks will need Lock, if at all, depending on Darnold’s status. But the Seahawks demonstrated they can win with their backup. — Destin

One reason the Patriots thought Wednesday might go differently from the Super Bowl — and why this team could be better than last year’s group — is that they added a true No. 1 wide receiver in A.J. Brown.

Now, they may be without Brown going forward.

Brown suffered an ankle injury early in the third quarter and limped back to the locker room for further evaluations before being ruled out. Since ankle injuries tend to linger, the Patriots could be without their big offseason acquisition for a couple of games.

But what made things worse is what happened after Brown left.

Romeo Doubs became New England’s No. 1 target. The Pats added the former Packer in free agency, and he had a strong training camp, especially in the red zone. But Doubs struggled on Wednesday.

Maye’s first interception came when targeting Doubs downfield, though that was more the result of a poor pass. Then, in the fourth quarter, Doubs, wide open with a chance to run downfield, dropped a would-be first-down pass. On the very next play, Maye threw his second interception of the night, which led to Seattle’s go-ahead field goal.

The Pats will be hoping for a quick recovery from Brown, and they need Doubs to bounce back from a rough debut. — Graff
